narrative: Material PL1__M6707BBC exhibits an intermittent/variable demand pattern (CV=0.535) with no statistically significant trend over the 132-day observation window. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.504, range 0.23–4.28 days), introducing substantial replenishment uncertainty. The combined sigma of lead-time demand (6,253 units) requires a safety stock of 10,287 units to sustain a 95% service level — nearly 10× the current SAP value. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with EOQ-based batch sizing reduces ordering frequency from ~368 to ~68 orders per year, saving $8,354 annually while maintaining full capacity feasibility at 38% storage utilisation.
warnings: SAP safety stock (1,033) is severely undersized for 95% SL — recommended value is 10,287 units (+896%)
Lead time instability (CV=0.504) classified as unstable — supplier SLA review recommended
High demand variability (CV=0.535) — periodic re-forecasting advised

research_insights.selection_rationale: The (r,Q) policy is appropriate for a material with intermittent/variable but predominantly non-zero demand (93% non-zero days), unstable lead times, and a clear MOQ constraint. Continuous review ensures the reorder point triggers replenishment as soon as inventory drops to 25,611 units, protecting against both demand spikes and lead-time uncertainty. EOQ determines the batch size, balancing ordering and holding costs optimally.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (69,325 units) is non-binding at 38.1% utilisation post-replenishment. No capacity-driven order reduction was required. However, if demand or safety stock estimates increase materially, the constraint could become active above ~53,000 units of combined safety stock + order quantity.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility. Escalation recommended for supplier lead-time instability (CV=0.504): consider dual-sourcing or supplier SLA penalties to reduce sigma_L and lower the required safety stock.
